title: Fourteen Summers and One Short Rain
subtitle: 气候变化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 气候变化（环境保护·气候变化）
meta: 主题语境：气候变化（环境保护·气候变化）　|　核心词汇：drought　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 drought 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my grandfather ① lived through a drought that no farmer in the valley would have named, and he said the living was the whole of the summer. The ② drought, meaning the season and not the shortage, ran fourteen summers and stayed unnamed in the book; a drought, he said, is the only thing in a valley that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ drought in that valley had the same short rain at the end of it, and the ④ drought at the end, meaning the one they kept for the river and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A drought, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to wait; my grandfather said the waiting is the part that fills fourteen summers.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the drought was the whole of the story, meaning the shortage and not the season. The ⑥ drought, meaning the shortage and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody talks about and nobody prepares for; drought, he said, is either something you live through or the only word that means both a season and a shortage. He said the shortage is the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ drought had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short rain. The ⑧ drought of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in July, was one valley and fourteen summers of waiting; drought, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to wait. She said the waiting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ drought I remember is the one named in the report, which broke in 1979 and is still described as the quietest in the valley. A ⑩ drought, my grandmother said in 1981, is the only one that improves by being waited out; every drought, she said, is a shortage that has agreed to look like a season. She said the shortage was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 旱灾；干旱（指那条河谷里遭遇的那一场）
B. n. 旱灾；干旱（指那场干旱本身，与缺水的状态相对）
C. 固定搭配：live through a drought 熬过一场旱灾
D. n. 旱灾；干旱（指留给河谷的那一场）
E. n. 旱灾；干旱（抽象总称，指一条河谷的旱情之事）
F. n. 旱灾；干旱（指年报上写到、被列名的那一场）
G. n. 长期缺水的状态（指故事里人人都谈论却无人准备的那样东西）
H. n. 缺水的状态（抽象总称，指人人都谈论却无人准备的那种状态）

items.q: lived through a drought that no farmer in the valley would have named
The drought, meaning the season and not the shortage
the drought was the whole of the story
the drought had become a line in a report
The drought of the whole thing
A drought, my grandmother said in 1981

answers.why: live through a drought 意为“熬过一场旱灾”，1958 年祖父熬过了一场河谷里没有一位农户肯说出口的旱灾。
drought 意为“旱灾、干旱”，指那场干旱本身而不是缺水的状态，它经过了十四个夏天而在簿子上没有名字。
drought 意为“旱灾、干旱”，指那条河谷里的每一场旱灾，每一场到头都有同一场短短的雨。
drought 意为“旱灾、干旱”，指留给河谷的那一场，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
drought 意为“长期缺水的状态”，指故事里人人都谈论却无人准备的那样东西，叔叔说这种缺水状态就是那个故事的全部。
drought 意为“缺水的状态”，指人人都谈论却无人准备的那种状态而不是那场干旱，是故事里人人都谈论、却无人准备的东西。
drought 意为“旱灾、干旱”，指年报上写到、被列名的那一场，到 1967 年这场旱灾成了年报里的一行。
drought 意为“旱灾、干旱”，祖父七月写道，整件事的旱情之事是一条河谷和十四个夏天的等待。
drought 意为“旱灾、干旱”，我记得的是年报上列名的那一场，1979 年结束了，至今仍被说成河谷里最安静的一场。
drought 为抽象总称，祖母 1981 年说，一场旱灾是唯一会因为被好好等待而变得更好的东西。

叔叔说这种缺水状态就是那个故事的全部，指的是缺水的状态而不是那场干旱。（drought）
